stem: A 6-year-old boy is examined because his parent says one testis keeps disappearing; on examination it can be milked into the scrotum and remains there for a substantial period. Which description best fits this finding?

options.text: Retractile testis due to a hyperactive cremasteric reflex
Ectopic testis lying outside the normal line of descent
Congenital undescended testis that cannot remain in the scrotum
Bell-clapper deformity causing excessive testicular mobility
Ascending testis that is no longer palpable in the scrotum

explanation: Retractile testis due to a hyperactive cremasteric reflex is the correct description. The testis can be brought into the scrotum and stays there for a substantial period, which distinguishes it from an undescended or ectopic testis.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Correct because a retractile testis is caused by a hyperactive cremasteric reflex and can be milked into the scrotum where it remains temporarily.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because an ectopic testis lies outside the normal line of descent and is not simply a testis that can be brought down into the scrotum.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because an undescended testis cannot be maintained in the scrotum after manipulation.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because bell-clapper deformity is associated with testicular torsion, not a testis that can be milked into the scrotum and remain there.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because an ascending testis has moved out of the scrotum over time and is not the same as a retractile testis that can be positioned back into the scrotum
